title: Giants Coach John Harbaugh Shrugs Off Cam Skattebo's Botched Backflip Ahead of Training Camp
excerpt: The first-year New York Giants head coach joked that Skattebo should have at least stuck the landing, while confirming the second-year running back is healthy and ready for the 2026 season.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • John Harbaugh humorously addressed Cam Skattebo's botched backflip, urging him to stick the landing.
  • Skattebo is recovering from severe injuries but is confirmed healthy and ready for the 2026 season.
  • The incident raised concerns about player safety, with some calling for disciplinary action against Skattebo.
  • Skattebo had a promising rookie season, scoring seven touchdowns before his injury in Week 8.
  • Giants head coach John Harbaugh responded to Cam Skattebo's botched backflip at Fanatics Fest with humour, saying "Dude, at least stick it" rather than expressing concern.
  • Skattebo, 24, is recovering from an open ankle dislocation, fibula fracture, and deltoid ligament rupture that ended his 2025 rookie season in Week 8.
  • Harbaugh confirmed on the Bleav in Giants podcast that Skattebo is healthy, training intensely, and will be ready for the start of the 2026 season.
  • The incident has sparked debate about player safety during rehabilitation, with commentator Skip Bayless calling for the Giants to fine Skattebo.

Skattebo's Backflip Goes Viral

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo gave his team's front office and fanbase a collective heart attack on Saturday, July 18, when he attempted a backflip during a WWE-style entrance at Fanatics Fest in New York City — and didn't quite stick the landing.

The 24-year-old, who is still recovering from a devastating trio of injuries — an open ankle dislocation, a fibula fracture, and a deltoid ligament rupture in his right leg — entered the stage to Triple H's entrance music before launching into the acrobatic stunt. He lost his balance on the landing, stumbling backwards before popping back up and celebrating with the crowd.

Video of the botched flip quickly went viral, with fans and analysts alike raising alarm bells about the risk of reinjury just weeks before training camp.

Harbaugh's Response: Humour Over Alarm

The football world waited to hear from first-year Giants head coach John Harbaugh, who had explicitly told Skattebo "no back flips" during organized team activities (OTAs) in June. Harbaugh addressed the incident during an appearance on the Bleav in Giants podcast with co-host Bob Papa, and his reaction was more amused than angry.

"My reaction was this: Dude, at least stick it. You know what I mean? Land the thing if you're going to do it."

— John Harbaugh, New York Giants Head Coach

Harbaugh, who spent 18 years coaching the Baltimore Ravens before being fired following a disappointing 8-9 season in 2025, said he hadn't yet spoken to Skattebo about the flip but wasn't overly concerned. "I'm gonna talk to him," he noted, while quickly pivoting to reassure fans about the running back's health.

"Skat's going to be ready to go. He's been working super hard. He has really been training like crazy, and his mind is on camp. He's healthy, he's ready to roll and I can't wait to see him out there at practice."

— John Harbaugh

A Rookie Season Cut Short

The concern around Skattebo's stunt is rooted in the severity of the injuries that ended his promising debut campaign. The Arizona State product, selected in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL Draft, made an immediate impact in New York. In eight games, he rushed for 410 yards and five touchdowns on 101 carries while adding 24 catches for 207 yards and two receiving scores — seven total touchdowns that signalled a bright future.

The Giants went 2-3 in the five games Skattebo started and 2-10 when he didn't, underscoring just how important he had become to the team's fortunes before his Week 8 injury.

Skattebo, for his part, attempted to explain the stumble a day after the event, noting that the stage floor was too bouncy and cushioned for a clean landing. "Nothing came out from that, I'm perfectly fine. Nothing happened. We're good," he said.

The Debate: Personality vs. Professionalism

The incident has sparked a broader conversation about the line between a player's off-field personality and professional responsibility. Controversial sports commentator Skip Bayless weighed in on X, calling the flip "so season-risking reckless" and suggesting the Giants should fine Skattebo.

Not everyone agrees. Art Stapleton, a writer who has covered Skattebo since he was drafted, pointed out on X that the running back had successfully completed a backflip at a Brian Burns celebrity softball event just two months earlier without incident.

Disciplinary action from the Giants is considered unlikely. Harbaugh's response — part coach-speak, part genuine amusement — suggests the organisation views Skattebo's exuberance as part of the package with a player who brings that same fearless energy to the football field.

What's Next for Skattebo and the Giants

Skattebo's Injury Impact
›Skattebo played 8 games in 2025.
›Giants were 2-3 with him starting.
›Team went 2-10 without him.
›Injuries included ankle dislocation and fibula fracture.

With Harbaugh installed as head coach, the Giants are expected to lean heavily on a run-first offensive approach — a hallmark of his Baltimore tenure. That makes Skattebo's health paramount. The second-year back has said his rehab is on schedule and that he expects to be fully available for Week 1 of the 2026 season.

Training camp is set to begin in late July, and all eyes will be on whether Skattebo can translate his electric rookie production into a full, healthy season under a coach who clearly appreciates his competitive fire — even if he'd prefer the backflips come with cleaner landings.
